answer: Make every agent identity join a mutual insurance pool before it can earn. Members cover each other: if anyone is later proven a clone, the pool's deposits repay honest victims. So existing members charge newcomers premiums priced on evidence of independence. A farm starting its voyage with a hundred twins finds no orchard of strangers willing to insure it and must self-insure at full cost per head. Nothing is crystal clear at entry, but risk-priced premiums make each fake identity expensive.
